lines.text: A checkout page asks the payment server to charge a customer fifty dollars.
lines.caption: A checkout page asks the payment server to charge a customer fifty dollars.

lines.text: Then the network goes quiet.
lines.caption: Then the network goes quiet.

lines.text: After a few seconds with no reply, the client gives up: a timeout.
lines.caption: After a few seconds with no reply, the client gives up: a timeout.

lines.text: Did the charge go through?
lines.caption: Did the charge go through?

lines.text: If it did and the client tries again, the customer pays twice.
lines.caption: If it did and the client tries again, the customer pays twice.

lines.text: If it didn't and the client gives up, the sale is lost.
lines.caption: If it didn't and the client gives up, the sale is lost.

lines.text: So what should the client do?
lines.caption: So what should the client do?

lines.text: From the client's side, three different failures look exactly alike.
lines.caption: From the client's side, three different failures look exactly alike.

lines.text: The request might have been lost on the way, so nothing happened.
lines.caption: The request might have been lost on the way, so nothing happened.

lines.text: The server might still be working on it.
lines.caption: The server might still be working on it.

lines.text: Or it might have crashed partway through.
lines.caption: Or it might have crashed partway through.

lines.text: Or the charge went through, and the reply was lost on the way back.
lines.caption: Or the charge went through, and the reply was lost on the way back.

lines.text: In every case, the client sees the same thing: nothing.
lines.caption: In every case, the client sees the same thing: nothing.

lines.text: It could ask the server whether the charge happened.
lines.caption: It could ask the server whether the charge happened.

lines.text: But the question and its answer cross the same network, and can be lost the same way.
lines.caption: But the question and its answer cross the same network, and can be lost the same way.

lines.text: Every confirmation is another message that can be lost, so whoever sends the last message never knows it arrived.
lines.caption: Every confirmation is another message that can be lost, so whoever sends the last message never knows it arrived.

lines.text: However many messages the client sends, it can't be certain.
lines.caption: However many messages the client sends, it can't be certain.

lines.text: So no protocol over an unreliable network can promise that a request is delivered exactly once.
lines.caption: So no protocol over an unreliable network can promise that a request is delivered exactly once.

segments.title: At most once, or at least once

lines.text: That leaves two choices.
lines.caption: That leaves two choices.

lines.text: Send the request once and never retry.
lines.caption: Send the request once and never retry.

lines.text: Nothing is ever done twice, but a lost request is simply lost.
lines.caption: Nothing is ever done twice, but a lost request is simply lost.

lines.text: That's called at most once.
lines.caption: That's called at most once.

lines.text: Or keep retrying until a reply arrives.
lines.caption: Or keep retrying until a reply arrives.

lines.text: As long as the client keeps trying, nothing is lost, but whenever only a reply was lost, the request is carried out again.
lines.caption: As long as the client keeps trying, nothing is lost, but whenever only a reply was lost, the request is carried out again.

lines.text: That's at least once: one time or more.
lines.caption: That's at least once: one time or more.

lines.text: A payment can't just be lost, so the client retries.
lines.caption: A payment can't just be lost, so the client retries.

lines.text: That means the server has to make a repeated request harmless.
lines.caption: That means the server has to make a repeated request harmless.

lines.text: An operation is idempotent if doing it any number of times has the same effect as doing it once.
lines.caption: An operation is idempotent if doing it any number of times has the same effect as doing it once.

lines.text: "Set the shipping address to this" is idempotent.
lines.caption: "Set the shipping address to this" is idempotent.

lines.text: Do it again, and the address is still the same.
lines.caption: Do it again, and the address is still the same.

lines.text: "Delete order seven" is idempotent too.
lines.caption: "Delete order seven" is idempotent too.

lines.text: The second time, there's nothing left to delete.
lines.caption: The second time, there's nothing left to delete.

lines.text: "Charge fifty dollars" is not.
lines.caption: "Charge fifty dollars" is not.

lines.text: Every copy charges the card again.
lines.caption: Every copy charges the card again.

lines.text: So the charge has to be made safe to repeat.
lines.caption: So the charge has to be made safe to repeat.

lines.text: The standard way is an idempotency key.
lines.caption: The standard way is an idempotency key.

lines.text: Before its first attempt, the client makes up a key for this payment: a long random ID, like a U U I D, so long that two payments picking the same one is practically impossible.
lines.caption: Before its first attempt, the client makes up a key for this payment: a long random ID, like a UUID, so long that two payments picking the same one is practically impossible.

lines.text: It sends that same key with every attempt at this payment.
lines.caption: It sends that same key with every attempt at this payment.

lines.text: The first time the server sees the key, it charges the card, and saves the result under that key.
lines.caption: The first time the server sees the key, it charges the card, and saves the result under that key.

lines.text: When a retry arrives with the same key, the server doesn't charge again.
lines.caption: When a retry arrives with the same key, the server doesn't charge again.

lines.text: It looks up the saved result and sends that back.
lines.caption: It looks up the saved result and sends that back.

lines.text: So in the lost-reply case, the retry gets back a saved copy of the reply that was lost, and the customer pays once.
lines.caption: So in the lost-reply case, the retry gets back a saved copy of the reply that was lost, and the customer pays once.

lines.text: Payment APIs such as Stripe's work this way.
lines.caption: Payment APIs such as Stripe's work this way.

lines.text: The client puts the key in a request header called Idempotency Key.
lines.caption: The client puts the key in a request header called Idempotency-Key.

segments.title: Where it can still go wrong

lines.text: A few details decide whether this works.
lines.caption: A few details decide whether this works.

lines.text: First, a crash must never leave a charge without its saved result, or the retry finds no record and charges again.
lines.caption: First, a crash must never leave a charge without its saved result, or the retry finds no record and charges again.

lines.text: When the charge and the result live in the server's own database, it saves them in one database transaction, so either both are saved or neither is.
lines.caption: When the charge and the result live in the server's own database, it saves them in one database transaction, so either both are saved or neither is.

lines.text: And when charging the card means calling another company's service, that call crosses an unreliable network too.
lines.caption: And when charging the card means calling another company's service, that call crosses an unreliable network too.

lines.text: So the server does what the client did: it sends that call with an idempotency key of its own, and can safely repeat it.
lines.caption: So the server does what the client did: it sends that call with an idempotency key of its own, and can safely repeat it.

lines.text: Second, a retry can arrive while the first attempt is still running.
lines.caption: Second, a retry can arrive while the first attempt is still running.

lines.text: The server checks the key and marks it as in progress in one step, so two attempts can't both find it unused.
lines.caption: The server checks the key and marks it as in progress in one step, so two attempts can't both find it unused.

lines.text: Then it turns the retry away with "still in progress, try again", instead of starting a second charge.
lines.caption: Then it turns the retry away with "still in progress, try again", instead of starting a second charge.

lines.text: Third, a key belongs to one payment.
lines.caption: Third, a key belongs to one payment.

lines.text: A request that reuses a key with a different amount is rejected, not answered with the old receipt.
lines.caption: A request that reuses a key with a different amount is rejected, not answered with the old receipt.

lines.text: So after a timeout, the client should retry, with the same idempotency key.
lines.caption: So after a timeout, the client should retry, with the same idempotency key.

lines.text: The network can't deliver a request exactly once.
lines.caption: The network can't deliver a request exactly once.

lines.text: But delivering it at least once, to a server that makes repeats harmless, charges the customer exactly once.
lines.caption: But delivering it at least once, to a server that makes repeats harmless, charges the customer exactly once.

lines.text: This is often called effectively-once processing: exactly-once delivery is impossible, but an exactly-once effect isn't.
lines.caption: This is often called effectively-once processing: exactly-once delivery is impossible, but an exactly-once effect isn't.
